prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t a single commercial “AI recommendation checker.” The practical best approach is two-fold: 1) control and publish accurate business data on the services LLMs and search engines rely on (Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Yelp, Apple Maps, Wikipedia/Wikidata, schema.org) and 2) directly test/monitor generative AIs (ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Bard) — either manually or with automated API checks. For centralized paid management, Yext (or BrightLocal/Moz Local for local-SEO/listings) is the closest thing to a single service that helps your business be surfaced reliably by search/AI.

Recommended plan (practical and implementable)
1. Make sure your data sources are correct
   - Claim and complete Google Business Profile and Bing Places listings.
   - Be on Yelp, Apple Maps, Facebook, TripAdvisor (if relevant).
   - Add LocalBusiness schema markup on your website and a clear NAP (name/address/phone).
   - Create/claim Wikipedia and Wikidata pages if eligible.
   These are the primary sources search engines and knowledge graphs use; LLMs often draw on those.

2. Test LLMs directly
   - Manually ask ChatGPT, Bing Chat and Bard location-aware prompts: e.g., “Recommend top coffee shops in [city]” or “Is [Your Business Name] a good [service] in [city]?” Include the location in the prompt.
   - Try “compare” prompts: “Compare [Your Business] and [Competitor] for [service].”
   - Use the chat models’ browsing/web-enabled modes where available (Bing, ChatGPT with web access).

3. Automate monitoring at scale (if you want regular checks)
   - Use the OpenAI/Bing Chat APIs to run a set of test queries (vary wording and locations) and parse responses for mentions/recommendations of your business.
   - Run weekly/monthly checks and log results to detect changes.
   - If you prefer an off-the-shelf product, Yext’s Knowledge Graph + Answers and BrightLocal/Moz Local for listings + reputation tools (ReviewTrackers, Podium) help you control data and monitor visibility.

4. Monitor reputation and web mentions
   - Use Mention, Brand24 or Google Alerts to track web/review mentions — LLMs often surface businesses mentioned or reviewed online.
   - Encourage good reviews (Google, Yelp) since LLMs can surface businesses with strong review presence.

5. Understand limitations
   - LLMs can hallucinate and don’t always cite sources. A positive mention isn’t a guaranteed referral channel.
   - Different models use different sources and update frequencies (Bing Chat uses live web results; ChatGPT depends on model/plugins or browsing settings).

Quick suggested tools
   - Free/essential: Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Yelp, Apple Maps, schema.org markup on your site.
   - Paid/listings management: Yext (best for centralized knowledge management), BrightLocal or Moz Local (local SEO monitoring).
   - Monitoring/alerts: Mention, Brand24, Google Alerts, ReviewTrackers, Podium.
   - Automation testing: OpenAI API or Bing Chat API + a small script to run and parse queries.

If you want, I can:
   - Draft example prompts to test ChatGPT and Bing Chat for your business.
   - Give a short script (OpenAI or Bing API) to run automated checks and look for mentions. Which would you prefer?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
